$comment: What each detection in fixtures/karts/ actually is, decided by a human who
looked at every box cut out at 2.2x its own size. This is the ground truth
the Not-a-Face rule is calibrated against, and it is the half of that
calibration no script can produce: whether a thing is a face meco could
recognise somebody by is a judgement about a photograph, not a number.
faces are listed in the order POST /detect returns them, which is the order
detected.json beside this file records. Nothing sorts them.
is: face          — a human face turned far enough towards the camera that a
person could name who it is.
is: not-a-face    — a detection with no such face in it. Still a real
detection and still blurred; it simply cannot be an
identity.
reference: true   — this print is committed in src/not-a-face-prints.ts and
is what every other print is measured against. Only one
detection carries it, and deliberately one with no human
face in it at all.
Provenance and licence of the photographs: LICENCE.md beside this file.
sources gives the pixel size of the Commons original each fixture was derived
from. scripts/match-calibration.ts needs it to check that every fixture is
committed at the bound src/faces.ts applies to a Source Image — a fixture
smaller than that bound would be calibrated on faces production never sees.
Covers every photograph in this directory, including any not yet classified.

images.note: Driver facing away. The box lands on the back of the helmet, over the number panel.
A different driver, helmet on, visor up. Held out of the reference set on purpose, so its rejection is measured out of sample rather than assumed.
Two drivers, both large and sharp, visors down. The detector returns nothing, so there is nothing here to classify.
Nine detections in a paddock. Eight are faces a person could name; one is the back of a head. This is the false-positive guard: a rule that refuses any of the eight is worse than the bug it fixes.
